message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  

**What you can do instead**

| Resource | How to use it | What it gives you |
|----------|---------------|-------------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂), forecast, and health advisories. |
| **EPA’s Air Quality Index app** | Download on iOS/Android. | Real‑time AQI, alerts, and historical trends. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Search “LA air quality” | Often publish daily summaries and health tips. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Look for “Air Quality” section. | Quick snapshot of AQI and pollutant levels. |

**Typical patterns in Los Angeles**

- **Spring & early summer**: Ozone peaks due to sunlight and traffic emissions.
- **Winter**: Particulate matter (PM₂.₅) can rise from heating sources and wild‑fire smoke (especially in the Southwest).
- **Overall trend**: LA usually stays in the “Moderate” (AQI 51–100) range most days, but occasional “Unhealthy” (AQI > 150) episodes can occur during heat waves or wildfire events.

If you’re planning outdoor activities or have respiratory concerns, it’s best to check one of the above sources right before you head out.
